Rotary Drill Operators, Oil and Gas, operate rotary drilling rigs at petroleum and natural-gas well sites. They control drilling, connect and replace drill pipe, manage drilling-fluid circulation, and record parameters as key operators on drilling crews.

entries: Oil and gas drill operators operate rotary rigs at petroleum and natural-gas well sites and control drilling, connect and replace tools, manage drilling-fluid circulation, and record parameters as key members of drilling crews.
Operate drilling rigs and control weight on bit, rotary speed, and rate of penetration.
Connect and replace drill pipe and tools and perform tripping and casing operations.
Monitor drilling-fluid properties and circulation systems and adjust parameters to procedure.
Record drilling parameters and well history and promptly identify and report anomalies.
Execute well-control and safety procedures and participate in emergency drills and response.
Maintain rig and well-site equipment and support crew shift handovers.

paragraphs: A 12-hour shift begins with inspection at handover: check the rig, mud pumps, and well-control equipment, then drill under the driller's direction. Monitor instruments and sounds while drilling. The entire crew coordinates during connections, and tripping is most physically demanding. The site is remote, and after work there is little beyond eating and sleeping until the next rotation.

This work suits people who tolerate remote wilderness, withstand shift work, and respect safety. Petroleum is industry's lifeblood, and you work on the front line.

This work carries the scale and drama of heavy industry: a rig dozens of meters high, roaring diesel engines, and a wellbore thousands of meters deep. One person at the controls influences the direction of the entire well. Office work cannot offer this kind of industrial grandeur.
